title: Weekend cutover playbook and post-release checks (Mar 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This playbook covers a typical weekend cutover for a medium-impact release (runtime + routing changes) where we expect a ~2–6 hour maintenance window for the slowest customers. It focuses on coordination, automated checks, manual verifications, and clear rollback criteria. Use this as a template and adjust times/owners for each release.

Pre-cutover (T-72 to T-2 hours) — ownership: Release Lead (Asha):
- T-72: Finalize and freeze the release branch. Ensure all PRs merged and green.
- T-48: Run full integration test suite against release branch. Post results to #release-ops.
- T-24: Notify affected stakeholders: CS, Platform, SRE, Security, Customer Success for any VIPs. Attach release notes draft.
- T-12: Provision cutover canaries in staging identical to production capacity (min 5% traffic). Validate end-to-end flows: auth, inference, console.
- T-6: Confirm infra quotas and bump if required (GPUs, IPs). Confirm DB migrations are scheduled and reversible.
- T-3: Final signoff meeting (15m) — Release lead, SRE lead, Product engineer, Dev lead. Record decisions and fallback plan.

Cutover day timeline (example weekend window) — timeframe adjustable per release:
- Fri 22:00: Pre-cutover snapshot/backup: take backups of config, DB snapshot if required, and export metric baselines.
- Fri 22:15: Lock deploy pipeline (no other merges). Switch on maintenance banner in Console docs (not customer-facing unless maintenance >2h).
- Fri 22:30: Warm up new model artifacts on staging and two canary clusters. Run quick perf regression script (token throughput / p95 latency).
- Fri 23:00: Begin progressive rollout to production canaries (2 clusters, 1% traffic). Monitor for 30m.
- Sat 00:00: Expand to 10% traffic if canaries OK. Run smoke-suite A (end-to-end generation and chat flows, embeddings sanity).
- Sat 01:00: Expand to 30% traffic and run smoke-suite B (session continuity, tool-calling, KV-cache behavior).
- Sat 02:00: Full ramp (100%) if all monitors green and no regression alerts from quality-monitoring hooks.
- Sat 04:00: Post-cutover validation window: run long-tail load sims for 60m, random prompt replay to detect drift.
- Sat 06:00: Final signoff. Announce release complete to stakeholders and update status page.

Roles & Contacts (ensure on-call paged before action):
- Release Lead: Asha Menon — overall coordination. Pager: asha@redwood, slack @asha.
- SRE Lead: Diego Ramirez — infra changes, rollback. Pager: diego@redwood.
- Platform/Runtime Owner: Karin Liu — runtime behavior, perf regressions.
- QA Lead: Noah Patel — smoke and regression test owner.
- Customer Success Liaison: Priya Shah — VIP customer comms.
- Oncall rotation: SRE Oncall Team — immediate mitigation.

Automated checks to run (pre- and post-rollout):
- CI pass (unit + integration): must be green.
- Perf baselines: token throughput within -15% of baseline or alert. p95 latency not exceed 1.3x baseline.
- Error budget check: last 7d error rate within allowed budget. If not, abort.
- Biz-level SLOs: latencies and successful inference % present in dashboard.
- Eval set regression: run the canonical prompt set and check for quality change > threshold (flag to ML owner).

Manual verification checklist (QA Lead):
- Core flows: generation, chat context retention, embeddings, reranking.
- Auth flows: login, token refresh, session continuity.
- Console: model list, rollout controls, metrics page loading.
- Observability: traces for sample requests show KV cache hits as expected and do not regress.
- Billing: token counts sensible for sample workloads.
- Edge-cases: long-context requests, tool-calling with large function args.

Rollback criteria (explicit triggers):
- Critical 5xx error spike >1% absolute over baseline for 15m.
- p95 latency > 2x baseline for 10m.
- Eval set quality degradation exceeding configured threshold (automated alert + ML signoff required to continue).
- Data-plane failures affecting >10% of clusters or any customer-reported data loss.

Rollback steps (Owner: SRE Lead):
1) Stop traffic to new variant via routing policy (automated canary abort).
2) Redirect traffic to previous stable model/version.
3) Mark release as aborted in tracker and notify stakeholders.
4) Collect logs and traces; begin RCA.

Post-release monitoring (first 72 hours) — owners: SRE + QA + Product:
- Hourly checks for first 6 hours: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, throughput.
- Every 4 hours until 24h: fine-grained correctness run of eval prompts.
- Daily summary at 24h and 72h to release channel with any deviations and actions.
- Customer Success: proactively check top 10 customers for anomalous usage or complaints.

Communications checklist:
- Pre-cutover (T-24): internal email to stakeholders with expected window and impact.
- During cutover: short updates every major step into #release-ops and pinned status page.
- Post-cutover: release announcement draft for public release notes and customer-facing summary.

Draft release notes (to be edited by Product):
- Title: Runtime & Router improvements — March 2026 release (beta features opt-in)
- Summary: This release improves inference throughput for mid-context workloads and includes routing policy fixes that reduce cold-start variance. Customers should see reduced p95 latency in typical conversational usage.
- Notable changes:
  * Serving runtime: new KV-cache eviction heuristics that reduce repeated attention recompute for long sessions.
  * Router: smarter fallback routing to quantized variants under constrained capacity to preserve latency SLOs.
  * Console: rollout UI now exposes canary traffic % and quick rollback action.
- Migration & compatibility: No client SDK changes required. Customers using pinned model versions are unaffected unless they opt into the new routing feature.
- Known issues and mitigations:
  * Small number of long-context sessions may see token-count inflation in logs (cosmetic) — fix in follow-up patch.
  * Embeddings micro-batch API may exhibit a slight throughput drop for batch sizes <4; workaround: bump batch size or use dedicated capacity.
- How to get help: file a ticket with customer support or escalate to Customer Success for VIP customers. For platform issues, ping #release-ops.

Postmortem and follow-up (T+3 days and T+14 days):
- T+3: Initial incident review if any issues occurred — owner: SRE Lead. Include timeline, decisions, and immediate fixes.
- T+14: Full postmortem for any production-impacting incidents with action items, owners, and target dates.

Checklist preflight summary (one-line signoffs):
- [ ] CI green (Release Lead)
- [ ] Perf/regression baseline check (Runtime Owner)
- [ ] Backups/snapshots taken (SRE)
- [ ] Stakeholders notified (Release Lead)
- [ ] Oncall paged and available (SRE Lead)
- [ ] Rollback plan agreed (Release Lead + SRE Lead)
- [ ] Customer Success informed of VIPs (CS Liaison)

Notes & Gotchas (lessons learned from past weekend cutovers):
- Always monitor deployment pipelining throttles — parallel deploys across clusters can cause API rate limits that look like regressions.
- Rolling back model artifacts is fast; rolling back routing/infra changes is typically slower — plan for this.
- Keep the first canary window long enough to surface memory leaks (30–45m).

Appendix: quick commands (replace placeholders)
- Cut traffic: /api/routing/set-variant?service=runtime&variant=stable
- Snapshot DB: pg_dump -Fc -v -f /backups/release_$(date +%F).dump

This doc is a template. Before any release, personalize: exact times, cluster names, runbook IDs, and escalation numbers. Save the customized copy under the release tracker and attach produced logs and timeline after the event.
